claims.text: A 26-year-old man with undiagnosed acromegaly presented to the emergency department with three days of progressive left eye vision loss and left retro-orbital pain, plus sudden right-sided weakness, dizziness and vomiting. Examination showed Glasgow Coma Scale 14/15, left eye light perception, third-degree left ptosis, right facial palsy and power of 1/5 in the right limbs with upper-motor-neuron signs.

claims.text: CT showed a sellar mass and left middle cerebral artery hypodensity, and MRI showed a large hemorrhagic sellar and suprasellar mass compressing the left internal carotid artery. claims.text: He underwent emergency transcranial craniotomy and tumor excision because of hemiparesis and visual deficit, leaving a small tuft of tumor behind. Histopathology confirmed pituitary adenoma with hemorrhagic infarction, and postoperative CT showed an empty pituitary fossa and a left cortical infarct. Diabetes insipidus developed on the third postoperative day, requiring desmopressin nasal spray, and thyroid hormones and steroids were supplemented. Hypothyroidism also developed postoperatively; the diabetes insipidus corrected eventually, but long-term thyroid hormone and steroid therapy was needed.
